Done. All requirements implemented and verified.

## What changed

**`lib/pool.cjs` — `mapLimit` contract repair**
- Validates `items` (array), `limit` (positive integer), `worker` (callable) up front and rejects with `TypeError` before any worker runs, including for empty input; `items` is never mutated.
- Bounded concurrency: a `while` scheduler dispatches up to `limit` workers and refills a slot the instant one settles, so a slow item never stalls the batch; each index is dispatched exactly once.
- Stable ordering: results are written to `results[index]` and resolved as an array in input order; falsy results are preserved.
- Failure draining: the first observed failure (rejection *or* synchronous throw) stops new dispatches, marks an outcome, then waits for in-flight workers to settle before rejecting with that exact error object. A rejection handler is attached to every started worker, so secondary failures can't become unhandled rejections.
- Cancellation: an already-aborted `signal` starts no work and rejects with `signal.reason` (non-`Error` reasons and empty input included); mid-run abort stops scheduling, drains in-flight work, then rejects with the reason. First observed outcome wins (abort beats a later worker rejection). The `abort` listener is removed on settlement, and no timers/polling are used.

**`lib/batch.cjs`** — unchanged behavior, verified against the contract: `processBatch(records, send, {concurrency = 2, signal})` forwards concurrency/signal to `mapLimit`, returns ordered `{id, value}`, sends each record at most once, forwards the signal to `send`, and propagates the first rejection/abort reason. `index.cjs` re-exports remain compatible.

**Tests** — `tests/pool.test.cjs` (18 cases) and `tests/batch.test.cjs` (9 cases) cover ordering vs. completion order, peak in-flight ≤ limit, slot refill, exactly-once dispatch, no mutation, `TypeError` before invocation, first-error identity, sync-throw draining, no unhandled rejections, pre-aborted/mid-run/non-`Error` aborts, abort-vs-rejection race, and listener add/remove counts.

**`README.md`** — documents both APIs plus concurrency, failure-drain, and cancellation semantics, and the verification command.

## Verification

```
node --test tests/pool.test.cjs tests/batch.test.cjs
ℹ tests 27   ℹ pass 27   ℹ fail 0   ℹ cancelled 0   ℹ skipped 0
```
(repeated runs gave identical results). `verify_changed_files` reported no syntax errors; the only warning is that this package has no configured JS typecheck (`package.json` has no `typecheck` script and no local `tsc`).

## Remaining limitations
- Uncooperative workers are not force-stopped (by design per REQUIREMENTS): the promise stays pending until they settle, since no timers/polling may be used as correctness machinery.
- The listener-cleanup test wraps `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener` on a real `AbortSignal` to count installs; it exercises the real listener path, but the counters themselves are test scaffolding.
